items.title: What the Trace Shows and What the Label Says: Auditing Behavioral Detectors in Agent Evaluation
items.summary_1line: LLM agents are often evaluated by reducing execution traces to labels such as final-answer correctness, tool verification, and fault propagation. These labels are measurements produced by parsers, behavioral detectors...
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, harness, evaluation.
items.editor_note: Frames trace labels (answer correctness, tool verification, fault propagation) as measurements that need auditing.

items.title: Memory or a Clock? Auditing a Memory Advantage in XLand-MiniGrid with Seeds, Maps and Evaluation Noise Apart
items.summary_1line: On a partially observable XLand-MiniGrid task, an LSTM agent beats a memory-free MLP by 25 percentage points. The gap looks like a clear case of memory. We ask two questions about it. First, how much of a measured gap...
items.editor_note: Applies the audit mindset to a reported LSTM-over-MLP gain of 25 points, separating seed, map and evaluation noise.

items.title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
items.summary_1line: For large language models (LLMs) and multimodal large language models (MLLMs), model-reported self-confidence is often miscalibrated, yet it may still be useful for efficient evaluation. At the same time, LLM-as-a-jud...
items.editor_note: Moves from diagnosing evals to a method: self-confidence and LLM judges to cut human audit cost.

editorial.tldr: Three papers in six days audit the measurements behind agent and model evaluation rather than the models. First came trace-derived labels, then a headline memory gain in XLand-MiniGrid.
editorial.whats_new: A new paper tests model self-confidence and LLM-as-a-judge as cheaper ways to audit human-in-the-loop evaluation, aiming for statistically sound accuracy estimates.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agent eval scores are only as good as the labels and noise floors behind them; if parsers, detectors, seeds or judges are unreliable, regressions and gains in your CI evals can be artifacts.
editorial.take_for_builders: Audit your own eval harness: spot-check detector labels against raw traces, rerun headline gains across seeds and maps, and calibrate any LLM judge against a human-labeled sample before trusting it.

beats.headline: Trace-derived labels are measurements, not ground truth
beats.summary: Behavioral detectors and parsers that turn agent traces into labels need their own audit.
